service.config_semantics: A config message may be sent first; the server echoes it back to confirm. If no config is sent, the server applies its own default values. A config sent mid-stream is ignored. One video file per invocation.
service.function_id_note: 15c6f1a0-3843-4cde-b5bc-803a4966fbb6 is the value printed in NVIDIA's eye-contact client README, which was fetched and read first-hand in this session. A separate UUID (7d09dd81-81ea-42ce-9909-843bdc07ec8d) was surfaced by web search against docs.nvidia.com but that page could not be fetched, and the search summaries themselves disagreed on whether it was NVIDIA's hosted function or a placeholder for a self-deployed one. The function id is therefore treated as a value to CONFIRM at execution time, not a settled constant; eval/maxine.py reads it from this spec so it can be corrected without touching code.

authentication.note: The environment variable name is this package's own choice; NVIDIA's sample client takes the key as a --api-key argument. GazeFix never places the key on a command line that could be captured in a process list or a log: see eval/maxine.py.

input_requirements.streaming_flag: --streaming is required when the MP4 has its moov atom before mdat (a 'streamable'/faststart file) and must be omitted otherwise; NVIDIA's client validates this and errors on a mismatch

known_client_defect.summary: NVIDIA's sample client catches every exception inside process_request and only prints it, so a failed inference can leave a truncated or empty output file while the process still exits 0.
known_client_defect.evidence: eye-contact/scripts/eye-contact.py, process_request(): 'except Exception as e: print(f"An error occurred: {e}")'
known_client_defect.gazefix_mitigation: eval/maxine.py treats a run as successful only when the process exits 0, the output file exists and is non-empty, no 'An error occurred' line appears on stdout/stderr, and (where ffprobe is available) the output probes as a decodable video stream.

evidence_for_available.verification: FIRST-HAND - fetched and read in full in this session
evidence_for_available.detail: NVIDIA's actively maintained client (SPDX headers dated 2025-2026) still documents 'Usage for Preview API request' with --preview-mode, --target grpc.nvcf.nvidia.com:443 and a concrete --function-id, and points at https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/eyecontact/api as the Try API. Grep across every fetched NVIDIA client source (README, eye-contact README, eye-contact.py, config.py, constants.py, utils.py, eyecontact.proto) found NO deprecation, end-of-life, sunset or retirement language.

evidence_against_available.verification: SECOND-HAND - web-search index summary only; the page itself is unreachable from this environment
evidence_against_available.detail: Three independently worded searches consistently reported the eyecontact model card carrying 'This API will be deprecated on 07/27/2026' and 'will no longer be supported after 07/27/2026', with advice to transition to another model. 07/27/2026 is approximately six weeks BEFORE today (2026-09-07), so if accurate and still in force the hosted preview API is already past its stated support end.
caveats: The page was never retrieved, so exact wording, scope and current force are unconfirmed.
build.nvidia.com uses this deprecation banner generically (an identically shaped notice was surfaced for an unrelated model), so attribution to eyecontact specifically is not proven.
A stated deprecation date is not proof the endpoint stopped responding, and NVIDIA may have moved the date.

hosted_availability.why_unresolved_here: Every nvidia.com host is denied by this container's organisation egress policy (gateway answered 403 to CONNECT), so no NVIDIA-hosted page could be read and no request could be attempted.
